extracted.intended_audience: writers, dramatists, storytellers, and students of narratology
extracted.subtask_description: A canonical taxonomy listing 36 fundamental dramatic situations, each stated with its necessary dramatic elements and a brief descriptive formulation and examples to guide plotting, characterization, and dramatic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a persecutor; a suppliant; a power in authority, whose decision is doubtful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suppliant appeals to the power in authority for deliverance from the persecutor. The power in authority may be a distinct person or merely an attribute of the persecutor (e.g., a weapon). The suppliant may also be two persons (Persecuted and Intercessor). Example: Esther interceding to the king on behalf of the Jews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverance
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: an unfortunate; a threatener; a rescuer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unfortunate has caused a conflict, the threatener is to carry out justice (or threaten harm), but the rescuer saves the unfortunate. Examples: Ifigenia in Tauride, Deliverance, Superman (1941 film).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime pursued by vengeance
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a criminal; an avenger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The criminal commits a crime that will not see justice through normal channels, so the avenger seeks justice by punishing the criminal. Example: The Count of Monte Cristo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vengeance taken for kin upon kin
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: Guilty Kinsman; an Avenging Kinsman; remembrance of the Victim, a relative of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two related figures (the Guilty and the Avenging Kinsmen) are put into conflict over wrongdoing to the Victim, who is allied to both. Example: Hamlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: punishment; a fugitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fugitive flees punishment for a (sometimes misunderstood) conflict. Examples: Les Misérables, The Fugitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a vanquished power; a victorious enemy or a messenger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The vanquished power falls from their place after being defeated by the victorious enemy or being informed of such a defeat by the messenger. Example: Agamemnon (play).

rubrics_metrics.name: Falling prey to cruelty/misfortune
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: an unfortunate; a master; or a misfortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unfortunate suffers from misfortune and/or at the hands of the master. Example: Job (biblical figure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revolt
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a tyrant; a conspirator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tyrant, a cruel power, is plotted against by the conspirator. Example: Julius Caesar (play).

rubrics_metrics.name: Daring enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a bold leader; an object; an adversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bold leader attempts to take the object from the adversary by overpowering them. Examples: Queste del Saint Graal; The Lord of the Rings; Raiders of the Lost Ark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: an abductor; the abducted; a guardian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abductor takes the abducted from the guardian. Example: Helen of Troy.

rubrics_metrics.name: The enigma
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a problem; an interrogator; a seeker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interrogator poses a problem to the seeker; the seeker must solve the enigma (often gaining ability or insight). Example: Oedipus and the Sphinx.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: (a Solicitor & an adversary who is refusing) or (an arbitrator & opposing parties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either a solicitor contends with an adversary who refuses to give an object in their possession, or an arbitrator must decide which opposing party receives the desired object. Example: the Apple of Discord.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enmity of kin
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Malevolent Kinsman; a Hated or reciprocally-hating Kinsman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Malevolent and Hated (or two mutually hating) kinsmen conspire together or oppose one another. Example: As You Like It.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rivalry of kin
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: the Preferred Kinsman; the Rejected Kinsman; the Object of Rivalry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Object of Rivalry chooses the Preferred Kinsman over the Rejected Kinsman, producing familial rivalry. Example: Wuthering Heights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Murderous adultery
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: two Adulterers; a Betrayed Spouse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two adulterers conspire to kill the Betrayed Spouse. Examples: Clytemnestra and Aegisthus; Double Indemnity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madness
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Madman; a Victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Madman goes insane and wrongs the Victim. Example: The Shining (novel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fatal imprudence
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: the Imprudent; a Victim or an Object Lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through neglect or ignorance the Imprudent loses the Object Lost or wrongs the Victim. Example: Kris Kelvin and his wife in Solaris (1972 film).

rubrics_metrics.name: Involuntary crimes of love
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Lover; a Beloved; a Revealer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Lover and the Beloved unknowingly break a taboo through their relationship, and the Revealer exposes this to them. Example: Oedipus, Jocasta, and the messenger from Corinth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slaying of kin unrecognized
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: the Slayer; an Unrecognized Victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Slayer kills the Unrecognized Victim (often leading to tragic recognition). Example: Oedipus and Laius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-sacrifice for an ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Hero; an Ideal; a Creditor or a Person/Thing sacrificed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hero sacrifices a Person or Thing for their Ideal; the sacrifice is then claimed by the Creditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-sacrifice for kin
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Hero; a Kinsman; a Creditor or a Person/Thing sacrificed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hero sacrifices a Person or Thing for their Kinsman, which is then taken by the Creditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: All sacrificed for passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Lover; an Object of fatal Passion; the Person/Thing sacrificed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Lover sacrifices a Person or Thing for the Object of their Passion, which is then lost forever. Example: Breaking Bad (2008 television show).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of sacrificing loved ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Hero; a Beloved Victim; the Necessity for the Sacrifice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Hero wrongs the Beloved Victim because of the necessity for their sacrifice. Example: the Binding of Isaac.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rivalry of superior vs. inferior
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Superior Rival; an Inferior Rival; the Object of Rivalry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Inferior Rival bests a Superior Rival and wins the Object of Rivalry. Example: Godzilla vs. Kong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adultery
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: two Adulterers; a Deceived Spouse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two Adulterers conspire or engage against the Deceived Spouse. Example: Brothers (2009 film).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crimes of love
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Lover; the Beloved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Lover and the Beloved break a taboo by initiating a romantic relationship (incestuous or otherwise forbidden). Example: Sigmund and his sister in The Valkyrie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of the dishonour of a loved one
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Discoverer; the Guilty One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Discoverer uncovers the wrongdoing committed by the Guilty One (often producing conflict or tragedy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obstacles to love
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: two Lovers; an Obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two Lovers face an external or internal Obstacle together. Example: Romeo and Juliet.

rubrics_metrics.name: An enemy loved
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Lover; the Beloved Enemy; the Hater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An allied Lover and a Hater have diametrically opposed attitudes towards the Beloved Enemy, producing conflicting loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: an Ambitious Person; a Thing Coveted; an Adversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ambitious Person seeks the Thing Coveted and is opposed by the Adversary. Example: Macbeth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict with a god
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Mortal; an Immortal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mortal and the Immortal enter into conflict (often involving fate, hubris, or divine will).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistaken jealousy
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Jealous One; an Object of whose Possession He is Jealous; a Supposed Accomplice; a Cause or an Author of the Mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Jealous One falls victim to the Cause or Author of the Mistake and becomes jealous of the Object, becoming conflicted with the Supposed Accomplice (or the supposed accomplice is wrongly suspected).

rubrics_metrics.name: Erroneous judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Mistaken One; a Victim of the Mistake; a Cause or Author of the Mistake; the Guilty One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mistaken One falls victim to the Cause or Author of the Mistake and passes judgment against the Victim when it should be passed against the Guilty One instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remorse
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Culprit; a Victim; or the Sin; an Interrogator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Culprit wrongs the Victim or commits the Sin, and is at odds with the Interrogator who seeks to understand the situation. Examples: The Bourne Supremacy, Memento.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery of a lost one
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Seeker; the One Found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Seeker searches for and eventually finds the One Found. Examples: A Very Long Engagement, Finding Nemo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of loved ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary elements: a Kinsman Slain; a Kinsman Spectator; an Executioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The killing of the Kinsman Slain by the Executioner is witnessed by the Kinsman Spectator, producing grief, revenge, or lament. Examples: Braveheart, Gladiator (2000 film).
